tagline: Build daily habits one streak at a time
summary: You want a lightweight daily companion for students: a list of small habits (water, reading, DSA practice) that can be ticked off in one tap, with streaks that make skipping a day feel like breaking a chain. The core loop is open → check off → feel progress.
problem: Students start habits with enthusiasm but lose momentum within a week because progress is invisible. Notes apps and generic to-do lists reset every day and don't reward consistency, so there's no reason to come back tomorrow.

targetUsers.description: Juggling classes, labs and hostel life, and trying to build routines like coding practice and exercise.
Needs daily consistency (one DSA problem, 20 pages of reading) more than intensity.
needs: A weekly view to spot missed days

features.name: Daily checklist
features.description: See today's habits and tick each one off with a single tap.

features.name: Streak tracking
features.description: Each habit shows how many days in a row it has been completed.

features.name: Create habits
features.description: Add a habit with a name, an emoji icon and a colour.

features.name: Delete habits
features.description: Remove a habit after confirming, so mistakes are easy to avoid.

features.name: Saved on device
features.description: Habits and history survive closing the app.

features.name: Weekly progress
features.description: A 7-day grid plus completion rate and best streak.

features.name: Daily progress bar
features.description: A header showing how much of today is done, with an encouraging message.

features.name: Daily reminders
features.description: A notification nudging you to check in each evening.

outOfScope: Push-notification reminders (needs notification permissions and scheduling)
Habits with custom schedules such as 3× per week
Social features like sharing streaks with friends
assumptions: Every habit is daily; a day counts as done once it is checked off.
A streak stays alive until the end of today, so an unchecked habit doesn't reset until tomorrow.
One person uses the app on one phone, so local storage is enough.
scopeNote: Reminders need push notifications, so v1 keeps everything on the device: habits and their history are saved with AsyncStorage, and the app starts with four sample habits so it feels alive on first launch.

clarifyingQuestions.question: If a day is missed, what should happen to the streak?
clarifyingQuestions.why: This decides how streaks are calculated and how forgiving the app feels.
options: Allow one rest day per week

clarifyingQuestions.question: Are habits always daily?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Custom schedules change the data model and make streak maths much harder.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What should the app feel like?
clarifyingQuestions.why: Sets the colour palette, typography and tone of the copy.

complexity.reasoning: Three screens, one data type and local storage — ideal for learning components, state and persistence without backend complexity.

platform.reasoning: One JavaScript codebase runs on Android and iOS, and Expo Go lets you test on your own phone instantly — perfect for an app you'll use every day.

alternatives.name: Flutter
alternatives.tradeoff: Excellent performance and UI toolkit, but you'd learn Dart instead of reusing JavaScript/React skills.

alternatives.name: Native (Kotlin / Swift)
alternatives.tradeoff: Best platform integration, but two separate codebases for Android and iOS.

alternatives.name: Progressive Web App
alternatives.tradeoff: No app store needed, but weaker offline storage and no native feel on iOS.

learningOpportunities: Breaking a UI into reusable components with props
Managing state with useState inside a custom hook
Saving data on the device with AsyncStorage
Building a validated form with TextInput
